wages.text: He supports higher wages, collective bargaining, the PRO Act, apprenticeships, and bringing good jobs back home.
wages.quote: I support higher wages, collective bargaining, the PRO Act, apprenticeships, and bringing good jobs back home.

debt.text: A group that asked him about its priorities reported that he is committed to protecting Social Security and Medicare.
debt.quote: Christian is committed to protecting these essential programs for seniors and all who depend on them.

housing.text: He says he would pursue policies to build and preserve affordable homes.
housing.quote: I will work for policies that help build and preserve affordable homes, and offer first-time buyers the help they need.

schools.text: He proposes universal pre-K, tuition-free community college and trade schools, and higher teacher pay.
schools.quote: In Congress, I will push to expand pre-K for every family, make community college and trade schools tuition-free, and pay our teachers what they are worth.

immigration.text: He says he supports border technology and enforcement alongside immigration-system reforms, without specifying either listed approach.
immigration.quote: I will support modern border technology, fair enforcement, and reforms that are needed to fix an immigration system that has failed the American people.

health.text: He supports Medicare for All and protecting Medicare for seniors.
health.quote: I support Medicare for All so an illness or accident doesn’t erase a lifetime of work.

voting.text: He has pledged to oppose voter suppression.
voting.quote: Christian has vowed to fight against all forms of voter suppression.

tax.text: He supported extending the 2017 tax cuts permanently.
tax.quote: This historic legislation permanently extends the 2017 tax cuts and prevents residents of Michigan’s 5th Congressional District from seeing a 27% tax hike.

wages.text: He voted against House passage of the 2019 Raise the Wage Act.
wages.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Raise the Wage Act Vote Type: Recorded Vote Status: Passed

trade.text: He called for free and fair trade policies and described the USMCA as a victory for Michigan workers and businesses.
trade.quote: We need trade policies that are free and fair and to enforce trade laws that keep our trading partners accountable.

debt.text: He says Medicare should be saved and strengthened for current and future beneficiaries.
debt.quote: We must keep our promise to the over 67 million Americans who rely on Medicare and work to save and strengthen Medicare for current seniors and future recipients.

schools.text: He supports expanding school choice and says federal scholarships should allow students to attend the school their families choose.
schools.quote: Michigan parents should have the opportunity to choose the type of education their children receive. If federal scholarships are made available to some students in failing schools, they should be allowed to attend the educational institution of their choice, free from government interference.

safety.text: He cosponsored fentanyl legislation that he says gives law enforcement additional tools to remove dangerous drugs from the streets.
safety.quote: ensures law enforcement has the tools needed to get these extremely dangerous drugs off our streets.

immigration.text: He supports border security and voted for legislation requiring ICE to detain certain immigrants accused of theft offenses.
immigration.quote: We must secure our borders, enforce our laws, and cut unnecessary red tape for legal immigration.

guns.text: He says he supports law-abiding citizens’ right to bear arms and has cosponsored concealed-carry reciprocity legislation.
guns.quote: I support the right for law abiding citizens to bear arms and will continue to defend this liberty throughout my service in Congress.

abortion.text: He says he will support legislation protecting the rights of the unborn and cosponsored legislation restricting federal funding for abortion.
abortion.quote: I will adamantly support legislative initiatives that preserve America’s founding principles and protect the rights of the unborn.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He supported legislation barring schools that receive federal funds from allowing transgender girls and women to compete in female sports programs.
gender.quote: schools and postsecondary institutions that receive federal funding cannot permit biological males to participate in athletic programs or activities designated for women or girls.

cannabis.text: He voted against House passage of the MORE Act, which would have decriminalized and descheduled cannabis.
cannabis.quote: Vote Question: On Passage MORE Act Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay Status: Passed

health.text: He introduced legislation to expand small businesses’ access to association health plans, which he says would increase choices and lower costs.
health.quote: By allowing small businesses to band together through association health plans, we can lower health care costs for working families.

energy.text: He supports expanding domestic energy production and opposes emissions rules he says would raise costs and limit consumer choice.
energy.quote: We must ensure that we do not implement unrealistic emissions rules that limit consumer choice, make life more expensive for families, and increase our reliance on foreign adversaries like China.

voting.text: He joined colleagues advocating for the SAVE Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register for federal elections.
voting.quote: The SAVE Act would require individuals to provide proof of citizenship, including REAL ID, when registering to vote in federal elections.

trade.text: He criticized U.S. policy for punishing industry and failing to form trade partnerships, and contrasted it with countries building commerce relationships.
trade.quote: The policy of The United States is war. At every turn we are regulating, blaming and punishing industry and not forming trade partnerships with the world.

trade.text: He says the U.S. needs tariffs on goods, phased in gradually and tailored to each country's trade balance.
trade.quote: This literally has to stop, and we don't really have a choice but to put tariffs on goods.

debt.text: He said balancing the budget is critical legislation and that he might oppose budgets containing items he considers unnecessary.
debt.quote: Critical legislation is to be balancing the budget. I might resist approving a budget if it includes items that aren’t necessary for our country, especially aid to foreign countries.

schools.text: He strongly opposed school choice and said tax money should remain with public schools.
schools.quote: All teachers want public schools and tax money should not be sent to private schools.

safety.text: He strongly disagreed with redirecting funds from police departments to community programs.
safety.quote: I support redirecting funds from police departments to community programs. Strongly Disagree

immigration.text: He called for strong borders and said immigration should follow current legal entry rules.
immigration.quote: Strong borders and especial concern for states that border Mexico

guns.text: He said automatic weapons should be limited.
guns.quote: What restrictions on gun ownership are needed to protect public safety? Automatic weapons should be limited.

abortion.text: He said his vote would phase out government intervention in women’s lives; in a questionnaire, he also said abortion should be allowed in all cases and the federal government should not limit it.
abortion.quote: My vote would be to phase out government intervention in a women’s life.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He agreed that biological males should not participate in women’s sports or occupy women’s spaces.
gender.quote: Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison. Agree

health.text: He selected the option supporting government-funded health insurance for anyone who wants it alongside private coverage.
health.quote: B. Our health care system is deeply flawed by our FDA. It is a profit oriented health system not a solution oriented health care system. Many treatments are not approved by the FDA which could save billions and reduce our medical costs.

energy.text: He strongly agreed that human-caused climate change is a global threat requiring urgent political action.
energy.quote: Man-made climate change is a global threat and requires urgent political action. Strongly Agree

voting.text: He disagreed that people should be able to vote without photo identification.
voting.quote: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Disagree
